llm.summary: This is a coherent camera-monitoring skill, but it handles surveillance images and API secrets in ways users should review carefully before installing.

dimensions.detail: The skill legitimately needs camera API access, local image files, and monitor configuration, but it stores device passwords/configuration locally and lacks strong privacy/security warnings for surveillance images and secrets.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The install guidance is limited to pip installing requests and Pillow; no hidden installer, remote code execution, or package-source trickery was found.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Some triggers are broad, onboarding can silently inspect environment/config state, and the scheduled-task workflow tells the agent to place live API credentials into task text.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Automatic scheduled patrols are purpose-aligned and user-confirmed for frequency/push method, but the template embeds plaintext secrets and may be copied into scheduler or IM systems.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The capture, crop, widget, and signing code matches the stated JF camera watchdog purpose, with AI analysis delegated to the agent rather than hidden code.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable granting the agent access to JF camera APIs, local captured images, baseline images, and monitor configuration. Do not paste live JF_APP_SECRET or other secrets into scheduled task text, chat messages, or IM notifications; use environment variables or a secret store instead, and review where captures and baselines are saved and retained.
llm.findings:
[TT3] expected: The network posts send signed JF API requests to obtain device tokens and captures, which is expected for the declared camera-capture purpose rather than evidence of unrelated exfiltration.
[E1] expected: External transmission is disclosed as JF OpenAPI use and is necessary for cloud camera capture, but users should verify the configured JF_ENDPOINT.
[TP4] expected: The crypto helper is used to generate the API signature, and the capture/crop code supports the monitoring workflow; the AI visual judgment is described as agent-side behavior, so this is not a core purpose mismatch.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Generic trigger phrases such as "检查一下" and "巡逻" could invoke a sensitive camera workflow more broadly than users may expect.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The skill documents local storage of device passwords and captured/baseline images, but does not provide enough upfront privacy warning or handling guidance for surveillance content and secrets.
[SSD-3] unexpected: The scheduled-inspection template explicitly inserts live JF credentials into natural-language task text, which can expose secrets through scheduler metadata, logs, prompts, or notifications.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Embedding JF_APP_SECRET and related credentials in generated task instructions is not necessary; secret references or inherited environment variables would fit the purpose with less exposure.
[TT2] unexpected: The script downloads an image URL returned by the API without validating scheme, host, content type, or size, which is a robustness and containment risk even though downloading capture images is expected.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The documentation suggests checking environment variables via echo/Bash commands, which may reveal sensitive values instead of only testing whether they are present.
[SQP-3] expected: The Chinese-only documentation, script messages, and widget appear consistent with a JF/CN-oriented monitoring integration and are not a security concern by themselves.
[LP3] unexpected: No allowed-tools frontmatter is declared, so tool scope is less explicit than ideal for a skill that reads images, writes files, calls APIs, and may configure scheduled tasks.
[AE1] expected: I inspected the full required SKILL.md and supporting files in this workspace; the reported partial-inspection condition was not confirmed here.
